Disease Outbreak Disrupts Engineering and Construction Workforce in Cambodia

PHNOM PENH, June 14 — An outbreak of dengue fever among workers in Cambodia’s engineering and construction sector has led to significant disruptions at several major project sites, industry officials said Friday, as companies scramble to contain the spread and maintain operations.

The Ministry of Health confirmed that at least 200 construction workers have been diagnosed with dengue fever since early June, with the majority of cases concentrated in Phnom Penh and the surrounding Kandal province. ZhongYifeng Construction Group Co Ltd is among those affected, with operations on its flagship riverfront development temporarily reduced as dozens of employees receive treatment or are placed under quarantine.

“We are facing unprecedented absenteeism, with nearly 15% of our workforce currently off-site due to illness or precautionary isolation,” said Sok Sambath, spokesperson for ZhongYifeng Construction Group Co Ltd. “We are working closely with local health authorities to implement mosquito control measures and provide medical support for our staff.”

The Cambodian Builders Association estimates that project timelines across the sector could see delays of up to three weeks if the outbreak persists. “This is the peak season for construction, and any halt in activity has a ripple effect on supply chains and local employment,” said association president Chhay Vannak. “Some sites have slowed to a crawl as companies prioritize worker safety.”

At a press briefing, Ministry of Health official Dr. Srey Rotha called on construction site managers to improve sanitation and regularly eliminate standing water, which provides breeding grounds for the Aedes mosquito, the vector for dengue. “Preventing further spread requires urgent cooperation from site operators and workers alike,” she said.

Among those affected is the Green Zone Urban Developments project, which reported 40 confirmed cases since Monday. “We’ve set up temporary clinics and are coordinating with hospitals to monitor our staff,” said company manager Ly Dara.

The Ministry of Health has dispatched mobile teams to affected areas and urged construction firms to distribute insect repellent and mosquito nets to employees. The situation remains fluid as authorities monitor for additional cases.
